svg.text: PART A - input conditioning: absolute values and result-sign flags
PART B - the 32-clock restoring divider: remainder / quotient shift registers, subtract, restore, counter
PART C - control: IDLE / BUSY state, 5-bit counter, stall
PART D - sign fix, divide-by-zero / overflow special cases, final selection
Fig P7b - RV32M (2/2): iterative divider (DIV / DIVU / REM / REMU), special cases and pipeline stall
Radix-2 restoring divider on magnitudes: 32 clocks. Signs are fixed before / after. Divide-by-zero and overflow follow the RISC-V spec (no trap).
Quotient is negative if the signs differ; the remainder takes the dividend's sign (RISC-V).
Unsigned DIVU / REMU: is_signed = 0, so neg_a = neg_b = 0 and nothing is negated.
Each clock while busy: trial = { rem[30:0], quo[31] }; diff = trial - divisor; if no borrow rem <- diff, quo <- { quo[30:0], 1 } else rem <- trial, quo <- { quo[30:0], 0 }.
(The mux inputs 'restore' / 'keep diff' implement the restoring step; start loads abs_a into the quotient register and clears the remainder.)
pipeline_stall = 1 freezes IF/ID (PC hold, Fig P1) and inserts NOP bubbles toward WB until done = 1; the result is then written once.
busy: set by 'start' (first cycle of a DIV/REM in EX), cleared by last_cycle. done = last_cycle (registered) or special-case bypass.
div_by_zero: DIV / DIVU -> all ones, REM / REMU -> the dividend. overflow (signed INT_MIN / -1): DIV -> INT_MIN, REM -> 0. No trap, as the RISC-V spec requires.
{overflow, div_by_zero} encodes the mux select: 00 normal, 01 divide by zero, 10 overflow. DIV / DIVU use funct3[1]=0, REM / REMU use funct3[1]=1.
In the special cases the divider is bypassed: done is asserted at once, so there is no 32-clock wait.
